trajectory_summary: A short, cooperative call that opened with real audio friction, moved efficiently through the verify sequence once the connection cleared, and ended in a clean hard DQ when the rep discovered the home was a manufactured home on a foundation — a category Ion doesn't work with. The rep's decision to hold and check before booking anything was the right procedural move; the call has no objection to resolve and no appointment to protect.

observed_outcome.quote: Hey. So it looks like we actually don't work with manufactured homes, so solar may not be the best option for you
observed_outcome.reasoning: The call ends in a hard disqualification after the rep confirms with a supervisor that manufactured homes on foundations are outside Ion's service scope; no appointment was booked or discussed.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured the $100 average bill figure but immediately moved to the next verify item ('have you seen a solar design for your home yet?') without reflecting it back or using it to build urgency; this became moot once the manufactured-home DQ ended the call minutes later, but the flip was not attempted.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The call was disqualified before reaching the bill-collection stage of the script; the rep never got to raising the actual utility bill document.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: There was an ad on the Internet that Colorado gave you 30,000 to put on solar.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: Customer gave a specific, quantified reason (a $30,000 incentive ad) but the rep relabeled it as 'the tax incentive' and moved to verify questions without circling back; this ties directly to the 00:47 cherry-pick moment and became moot once the call ended on the unrelated manufactured-home DQ.
